rule.name: ReplaceWithWrongLiteralKind
rule.message: String.replace takes plain text and replaceAll and replaceFirst take a regex, and this call mixes them up. replace("\\s+", "") looks for the three characters \s+ and removes nothing; replaceAll(".tmp", "") treats the dot as any character; replaceAll("?", value) throws PatternSyntaxException; and a File.separator or a backslash or dollar sign in the replacement is read as an escape or a group reference, which breaks on Windows. Use replaceAll for a regex (path.replaceAll("\\s+", "")), replace for text (sql.replace("?", value), file.replace(".tmp", "")), and Matcher.quoteReplacement(File.separator) for a replacement. An exception fits text that really contains the escape characters.
